source_text: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὑπέμεινεν ὁ κύριος παραδοῦναι τὴν σάρκα εἰς καταφθοράν, ἵνα τῇ ἀφέσει τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἁγνισθῶμεν, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ῥαντίσματος αὐτοῦ. γέγραπται γὰρ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἅ μὲν πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ, ἃ δὲ πρὸς ἡμᾶς, λέγει δὲ οὕτως: Ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν: τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν: ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἄφωνος ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτόν. οὐκοῦν ὑπερευχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι καὶ τὰ παρεληλυθότα ἡμῖν ἐγνώρισεν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐνεστῶσιν ἡμᾶς ἐσόφισεν. καὶ εἰς τὰ μέλλοντα οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀσύνετοι. λέγει δὲ ἡ γραφή: Οὐκ ἀδίκως ἐκτείνεται δίκτυα πτερωτοῖς. τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι δικαίως ἀπολεῖται ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ἔχων ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης γνῶσιν ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὁδὸν σκότους ἀποσυνέχει. ἔτι δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ἀδελφοί μου: εἰ ὁ κύριος ὑπέμεινεν παθεῖν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν, ὢν παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου κύριος ᾧ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ̓ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν: πῶς οὖν ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὸ χειρὸς ἀνθρώπων παθεῖν; μάθετε. οἱ προφῆται, ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἔχοντες τὴν χάριν, εἰς αὐτὸν ἐπροφήτευσαν: αὐτὸς δέ, ἵνα καταργήσῃ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν δείξῃ, ὅτι ὲν σαρκὶ ἕδει αὐτὸν φανερωθῆναι, ὑπέμεινεν, ἵνα τοῖς πατράσιν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν ἀποδῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ τὸν λαὸν τὸν καινὸν ἑτοιμάζων ἐπιδείξῃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤν, ὅτι τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτὸς ποιήσας κρινεῖ. πέρας γέ τοι διδάσκων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ καὶ τηλικαῦτα τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ποιῶν ἐκήρυσσεν, καὶ ὑπερηγάπησεν αὐτόν. ὅτε δὲ τοὺς ἰδίους ἀποστόλους τοὺς μέλλοντας κηρύσσειν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον αὐτοῦ ἐξελέξατο, ὄντας ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνομωτέρους, ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἦλθεν καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς, τότε ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ. εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἦλθεν ἐν σαρκί, οὐδ’ ἄν πως οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐσώθησαν βλέποντες αὐτόν, ὅτε τὸν μέλλοντα μὴ εἶναι ἥλιον, ἔργου τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχοντα, ἐμβλέποντες οὐκ ἰσχύουσιν εἰς τὰς ἀκτῖνας αὐτοῦ ἀντοφθαλμῆσαι: οὐκοῦν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τοῦτο ἐν σαρκὶ ἦλθεν, ἵνα τὸ τέλειον τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀνακεφαλαιώσῃ τοῖς διώξασιν ἐν θανάτῳ τοὺς προφήτας αὐτοῦ. οὐκοῦν εἰς τοῦτο ὑπέμεινεν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τὴν πληγὴν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐξ αὐτῶν: Ὅταν πατάξωσιν τὸν ποιμένα ἑαυτῶν, τότε ἀπολεῖται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης. αὐτὸς δὲ ἠθέλησεν οὕτω παθεῖν: ἔδει γάρ, ἵνα ἐπὶ ξύλου πάθῃ. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφητεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ. Φεῖσαί μου τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπὸ ῥομφαίας, καί: Καθήλωσόν μου τὰς σάρκας, ὅτι πονηρευομένων συναγωγαὶ ἐπανέστησάν νέστησάν μοι. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἰδού, τέθεικά μου τὸν νῶτον εἰς μάστιγας, τὰς δὲ σιαγόνας εἰς ῥαπίσματα. τὸ δὲ πρόσωπόν μου ἔθηκα ὡς στερεὰν πέτραν.
pass_a_gloss: For to this end the Lord endured to deliver his flesh to destruction, so that by the forgiveness of sins we may be purified, which is in the blood of his sprinkling. For it is written about him, some things to Israel, and some to us, and he says thus: He was wounded because of our iniquities and bruised because of our sins; by his stripe we were healed. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before the one shearing him. Therefore we ought to be very thankful to the Lord, because he made known to us also the things that have passed and in the present things he has made us wise. And we are not without understanding about the things to come. And the scripture says: The nets are not spread in vain for the winged creatures. This it says, that justly a man will perish, who having the knowledge of the way of righteousness turns himself to the way of darkness. And yet, my brothers, if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, being the Lord of all the world, to whom God said from the foundation of the world: Let us make man according to our image and likeness; how then did he endure to suffer by the hand of men? Learn. The prophets, having the gift from him, prophesied about him; and he, so that he might abolish death and show the resurrection from the dead, because it was necessary for him to be revealed in the flesh, endured, so that to the fathers he might give the promise, and he himself, preparing for himself a new people, might show on the earth that, having made the resurrection, he will judge. For teaching the end to Israel and doing so great signs and wonders, he preached and loved him exceedingly. But when he chose his own apostles, who were going to preach his gospel, being more lawless than all sin, so that he might show that he did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, then he revealed himself to be the Son of God. For if he had not come in the flesh, men would not have been saved by seeing him, when they cannot even look at the sun, which is a work of his hands, because they are not able to gaze at its rays. Therefore the Son of God came in the flesh for this purpose, so that he might sum up the perfect things of sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. Therefore for this reason he endured. For God says the stroke of his flesh is from them: When they strike their own shepherd, then the sheep of the flock will be destroyed. But he himself willed to suffer thus; for it was necessary for him to suffer on the wood. For the one prophesying about him says: Spare my soul from the sword, and: Pierce my flesh, because the assemblies of the wicked have risen up against me. And again he says: Behold, I have set my back for scourges, my cheeks for slaps. And I have set my face like a hard rock.

bible_refs.note: He was wounded because of our iniquities
Like a sheep he was led to slaughter
When they strike their own shepherd

pass_b_english: The Lord endured death so that through the forgiveness of sins we might be purified by the blood of his sprinkling (Isaiah 53:5). Scripture says of him, some things to Israel and some to us: He was wounded for our iniquities and bruised for our sins; by his stripe we were healed. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer (Isaiah 53:7). Therefore we ought to be deeply thankful to the Lord, because he revealed the past to us and has made us wise in the present, and we are not ignorant about the future. Scripture declares: The nets are not spread in vain for the winged (Zechariah 13:7); this means a person perishes justly who, having known the way of righteousness, turns to the way of darkness.

My brothers, if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, though he is Lord of all the world — the one to whom God said from the foundation of the world, "Let us make man in our image and likeness" — how then did he endure to suffer at human hands? Learn this: the prophets, gifted by him, prophesied about him; and he, to abolish death and reveal the resurrection from the dead, endured because he had to be manifested in the flesh. He endured to give the promise to the fathers, and while preparing a new people for himself, he would show on earth that, having brought the resurrection, he will judge. He taught Israel to the end, performing such great signs and wonders, and he loved them exceedingly. But when he chose his own apostles to preach his gospel — men more lawless than all sin — he did so to show he came not to call the righteous but sinners; then he revealed himself as the Son of God.

For if he had not come in the flesh, no one would have been saved by seeing him; human beings cannot even gaze at the sun, a work of his hands, because they cannot withstand its rays. Therefore the Son of God came in the flesh to sum up the perfection of sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. Therefore he endured. God says the stroke of his flesh is from them: "When they strike their own shepherd, the sheep of the flock will be destroyed" (Zechariah 13:7). Yet he himself willed to suffer thus, for he had to suffer on the wood. The prophet says of him: "Spare my soul from the sword," and "Pierce my flesh, because assemblies of the wicked have risen against me." And again: "Behold, I have given my back to scourges, my cheeks to slaps, and I have set my face like a hard rock."

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal translation, while Pass B provides a more fluent version with necessary scripture citations. All citations (Isaiah 53:5, Isaiah 53:7, Zechariah 13:7) correctly identify the quoted or alluded-to passages. The distinction in 'ὑπερευχαριστεῖν' (to be very thankful) and 'ἀνομωτέρους' (more lawless) is correctly handled.
